column1: # THE SIX BLOCKED ROWS, WORKED THE DAY THE BLOCK LIFTED — AND MOTA IS AN AFRICAN SURNAME.
# National Archives of South Africa, the NARSA Search Portal. Rows 137, 138, 140, 154, 175 and 275.
# Read 11 October 2026, the same day the service was found alive at its new address.
field
*** 278 RECORDS, AND THE NAME IS A FALSE LEAD FOR A REASON NOBODY HAD GUESSED ***
column2: row 137 called MOTA "the most important untested name" because MOTA FIGUEIREDO is the fullest form anybody wrote of Ivone's maiden name, and because 288 records was far past the harvest cap used on the other spellings. ALL OF THEM ARE NOW READ — 278 under the current index. *** MOTA IN THE SOUTH AFRICAN ARCHIVES IS OVERWHELMINGLY A SOTHO, TSWANA AND NGUNI SURNAME, NOT A PORTUGUESE ONE. *** The bulk of the 278 are NATIVE ESTATE files and magistrates' case files from the Free State and the Witwatersrand — Lehlohonolo, Litaba, Mohasoa, Sophoniah, Mbuti Meshack, Mngoqibelo Alfred, Maphehello Agnes, Monamoholo Johane — and criminal records. The depots split TAB 139, SAB 60, VAB 46, NAB 15, KAB 13.

column1: *** EIGHTEEN ARE PORTUGUESE AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS HERS ***
column2: TAB MHG 5905/69 "DA MOTA, JOAO" · SAB BVE 413 W4/117 "J di Caires da Mota" · KAB IRC 1/3/77 E38/78 "Immigration papers. Manuel Jose da Mota" · KAB IRC 1/3/76 E4/78 "Immigration papers. Manuel Francisco da Mota Veiga e Costa" · SAB URU 7110 2097, the recognition of Dr Carlos Teixeira da Mota as Portuguese consul-general in Johannesburg · two Brazilian diplomats named Silveira de Mota · and nine Witwatersrand court files for Joaquim Alves da Mota, Francisco da Mota Lopes, Maria Fernanda da Mota Rodrigues and Jose Fernando Seabra Mota Martins. NOTHING CONNECTS ANY OF THEM TO IVONE, and none is at Lourenço Marques.

column1: *** AND THE TWO-KEYWORD TEST SETTLES IT IN ONE LINE ***
column2: MOTA *and* FIGUEIREDO together return EXACTLY ONE RECORD across all twenty repositories: TAB WLD 1950/1948, her own first divorce, which this archive has held since September. MOTA and MARQUES: zero. FIGUEIREDO and LOURENCO: zero. THE ROW IS CLOSED AND THE ANSWER IS NO.

column1: the one estate worth naming, and it is named as a negative
column2: TAB MHG 5905/69, "DA MOTA, JOAO", is the ONLY Portuguese Mota estate in the whole index. A South African estate file carries form J294, which asks for the deceased's parents, so it is the shape of document this archive wants. IT IS NOT HERS AND NOTHING SUGGESTS IT IS. Recorded so the next person does not rediscover it as a hope.

column1: # ---------------- ROW 175: THE NUMBER THIS ROW WANTED, AND IT WAS NOT WHERE THE ROW SAID TO LOOK ----------------
*** TAB WLD 1878/1956 — AND THE ROW'S OWN SEARCH PLAN WOULD NEVER HAVE FOUND IT ***
column2: row 175 asked for the WLD number of "Kurt versus Frances, 1957" and said to search "NAAIRS, when it is back, under LUWINSKI, LUWINSKY and LUWENSKI". The file is indexed under NONE of them in a way those queries return — it was found under HOSTOWSKY, her maiden name. The row also had the year wrong: IT IS 1956, the year of the marriage. See correction 9500919.

column1: and the row predicted its own trap and still fell into it
column2: its last line reads "AND NOTE THE NEIGHBOUR ALREADY IN THE TABLE: WLD 2542/1957, Standard Bank versus K. Luwinski, sits in the same window." THAT NEIGHBOUR IS WHERE THE 1957 CAME FROM. The row saw the conflation, wrote it down as context, and did not notice it was the source of the date it was trying to confirm.

column1: # ---------------- ROW 138: SALKOW, AND ONE FILE THE ARCHIVE DOES NOT HAVE ----------------
eighty-nine SALKOW records, and the six this row listed are all confirmed
column2: TPD 5/901 467/1950 (Rosaline born Bernhardt v Morris Isaac) · WLD 2225/1953 (him v Ivonne, born DE FIGUERIDO) · TPD 2854/1960 (him v Rosaline Burns) · WLD 1593/1962 (him v Gertie, formerly Moagus, BORN AMBROSE — a maiden name this row did not carry) · WLD 3317/1963 (him v Cecilia Maud born Shein) · WLD 15934/1979 (Mayveen Properties v him). And the estate, KAB MOOC 6/9/5171 ref 61416, WHICH THE INDEX WRITES "SALKOW, ISAAC MORRIS" — the forenames reversed from every court file.

column1: *** AND A SEVENTH FILE, NEW: TAB WLD 2462/1966 ***
column2: ILLIQUID CASE. DIVORCE. ISAAC LEWIS BENJAMIN VERSUS ROSALINE EVE (BORN BERNHARDT, FORMERLY (1) BURNS (2) SPENCER-WILSON (3) SALKOW). Her FOURTH marriage ending, and the first record to give her a second forename: ROSALINE EVE.

column1: *** AND THE TWO FILES DISAGREE ABOUT THE ORDER OF HER MARRIAGES ***
column2: the 1960 title reads "ROSALINE BURNS (FORMERLY SPENCE-WILSON, FORMERLY SALKOW)" — which in the ordinary convention means Burns now, Spence-Wilson before, Salkow before that. The 1966 title NUMBERS them "(1) BURNS (2) SPENCER-WILSON (3) SALKOW", which puts Salkow last. THEY CANNOT BOTH BE RIGHT AND THIS ARCHIVE PICKS NEITHER. Note also SPENCE-WILSON in 1960 and SPENCER-WILSON in 1966.

column1: and one thing the row already knew is worth restating
column2: Morris Isaac Salkow married at least four times and Ivone was the second. She married him on 13 February 1953 and he sued her the same year, WLD 2225/1953. THE SAME SHAPE AS KURT AND FRANCES: married February, sued before the year was out.

column1: # ---------------- ROW 154: PAULINE, AND THERE IS NO THIRD ----------------
both references confirmed and the search is exhausted
column2: TAB WLD 583/1944, "PAULINE MILLER (BORN RAPPOPORT) VERSUS JOSEPH", and TAB WLD 332/1952, "PAULINE BERMAN (BORN RAPPOPORT) (FORMERLY MILLER) VERSUS ISRAEL". SEVENTY-FIVE RAPPOPORT RECORDS IN ALL TWENTY REPOSITORIES AND THOSE ARE THE ONLY TWO THAT ARE HERS. So: Joseph Miller, divorced 1944; Israel Berman, divorced 1952; Kurt after that. NO FOURTH HUSBAND AND NO FIFTH, on this index.

column1: # ---------------- ROW 140: EVERY CITATION RE-VERIFIED, AND THE WAY IT HAD TO BE DONE IS THE FINDING ----------------
*** A REFERENCE CODE IS NOT SEARCHABLE ON THIS SERVICE. AT ALL. ***
column2: the obvious way to re-verify a citation is to search the reference. IT DOES NOT WORK. "61416" returns ZERO while ZA KAB MOOC_6/9/5171_61416_1 sits in the index; and "534/1948" returns NINE THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED AND SIXTY-NINE records, because the keyword box TOKENISES ON THE SLASH and matches 534 OR 1948 anywhere in a title. The portal searches the TITLE TEXT and the reference code is not in it.

column1: so every citation was re-verified BY SURNAME, which is the only way
column2: and all of them came back with the reference code this archive already held: TPD 534/1948 · WLD 1950/1948 · WLD 2545/1950 · WLD 497/1951 · WLD 2368/1951 · WLD 2542/1957 · WLD 2451/1972 · MHG 7584/69 · MHG 4267/57 · MOOC 6/9/5171 61416 · WLD 2225/1953 · TPD 467/1950 · TPD 2854/1960 · WLD 1593/1962 · WLD 3317/1963 · WLD 15934/1979 · WLD 583/1944 · WLD 332/1952. ROW 140 IS DONE: NOT ONE CITATION IN THIS ARCHIVE IS STALE, and the sources page now prints the working address.

column1: # ---------------- AND A NEW SPELLING, OFF THE ARCHIVE'S OWN MOST-CITED FILE ----------------
*** DE FIGUEITEDO — A T WHERE THE R BELONGS ***
column2: TAB TPD 5/795 534/1948 is Ivone's FIRST divorce, from Johannes Antonie Oelofse de Witt, and this archive has cited it since September. ITS INDEX TITLE READS "JOHANNES ANTONIE OELOFSE DE WITT VERSUS YVONNE (BORN DE FIGUEITEDO)." Nobody here had ever recorded that spelling, because nobody had read the title — the file was known by its number. SEVENTEEN FORMS OF HER MAIDEN NAME ARE NOW ON /names/ AND THE NEWEST ONE WAS ON A DOCUMENT THE ARCHIVE ALREADY OWNED.

column1: the general lesson, which is the same one twice today
column2: A CITATION IS NOT A READING. Row 203's Spier household had been read and the row did not know; this file's title had been cited and never read. Both are the same fault: the archive records what it went looking for and not what the record said beside it.

column1: no bot gate, and the controls are in the companion file
column2: every query was one surname in one keyword box against repository RSA, issued from the portal's own page, with SMITH (47,936) and SCHMIDT (3,418) as live controls. The instrument's own measurements are in data/naairs-is-back-2026-10-11.tsv.
